messages:
Anita: Hi team — customer (FinTech POC) wants a private-deploy proof-of-concept. Key asks: preserve client source IP to backend, support TLS inspection in DMZ, and avoid public egress where possible. Can we confirm recommended topology and rough pricing delta (PrivateLink vs peering + NAT/EIP)?
Raj: quick answer: PrivateLink keeps control plane out of customer VPC and gives interface endpoints; peering is simpler but exposes route table surface. Preserving source IP is easier with an L4 proxy in-customer or with NLB + proxy.
Kevin: If they require TLS inspect in DMZ, typical pattern is: onprem -> egress proxy (TLS-inspect) -> NAT/EIP -> Redwood Private endpoint. That preserves client IP only if proxy forwards via X-Forwarded-For or if you do 1:1 NAT. Usually we don't get true source IP end-to-end without a proxy doing it.
Maria: Adding checklist items for the POC — please confirm these with customer: 1) CIDR(s) for spokes; 2) FQDN allowlist for egress; 3) whether they'll accept interface endpoints (PrivateLink) or prefer VPC peering; 4) expected concurrent rps and p95 latency SLO; 5) SOC2/PCI notes for TLS-inspect box.
Anita: They pushed back on adding a proxy because of latency. They asked if we can host an endpoint in their VPC (PrivateLink) and keep all egress inside their network — essentially, no public internet egress from traffic path. Thoughts?
Raj: PrivateLink endpoints are still cross-account interface ENIs; traffic to Redwood can stay within the region via AWS PrivateLink — no public IP required. However, if the customer wants to do TLS inspection, that must happen before traffic reaches the endpoint (so onprem or a DMZ proxy). PrivateLink doesn't magically remove the need for their TLS-inspect cluster.
Kevin: Cost note: PrivateLink = per-hour endpoint + per-GB data processing. Peering + NAT = NAT gateway cost (per-hour + per-GB) or managed proxy cost if they run HA proxies. For low-throughput proofs, PrivateLink often ends up cheaper and simpler. For sustained high throughput, dedicated NAT or egress appliances could be cheaper.
Maria: Sample firewall / SG snippet customers ask for (ask netops to verify):
```
# allow outbound to Redwood-private endpoints
aws_vpc_cidr: 10.10.0.0/16
allow_to_endpoints:
  - tcp:443
  - tcp:80
# if using EIP for legacy proxy
allow_to_eip: [34.201.11.22/32]
```
Kevin: Also send them the minimal TCP ports we need: 443 and 80 for health checks. If they run active health checks from multiple AZs we may need to document our endpoint subnet ranges — share list of Redwood-private endpoint IPs (we'll provide once POC onboarded).
Anita: Security questionnaire partial answer draft — please review before I send: "We support Private VPC deployments via AWS PrivateLink or VPC Peering. Customers can require TLS inspection with their onprem/DMZ proxies; Redwood Private does not perform customer TLS inspection inside the customer perimeter. We provide audit logs, KMS integration, and VPC-level endpoint controls."
Raj: Suggest adding: "For source IP preservation: we recommend either (a) an L4 pass-through proxy managed by the customer, or (b) header forwarding in an L7 proxy. Redwood can accept X-Forwarded-For headers for identifying client IPs in application logs."
Maria: Action items: - @Anita: confirm which topology they prefer (PrivateLink vs peering) and get CIDR + expected throughput. - @Kevin: prepare estimated cost delta for 1k RPS sustained vs 50 RPS POC (include NAT GW vs PL pricing). - @Raj: draft short blurb for the security questionnaire about egress/inspection.
Kevin: I'll drop cost bullets by EOD. For the POC we can offer a temporary EIP pool for easier allowlist testing — that'll reduce their work to a small firewall change.
Anita: Awesome. Customer next call Thu 10am PT. I'll bring the CIDR and say we'll prep a one-page network playbook. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Support ticket created: #POC-8421 — attach network playbook once ready.
Raj: adding a small caveat — if they want cross-region PrivateLink for DR, costs scale and replication patterns differ. We'll call that out in playbook. :eyes:
Maria: I'll assemble the one-page playbook + security Q draft now and share in this thread when done.
